findings.description: The pre-flight warns 'references file X not in diff post-image' for every exempt file (binary, rename, or mode-change), which verify does not refuse, producing a false alarm on every review that touches one.
The fabricated-lines algorithm exists twice, verbatim, in verify.py and receipt.py; only the variable names and the final line differ, so the two copies must be kept in lockstep by hand.

The exempt-file guard has no test: reverting the `if file_lines is None: continue` line to the old `.get(..., {})` leaves all 97 tests green while every review containing a binary, rename, or mode-change file would fail verify.

The A4 comment claims 'Duration collapse (all passes same wall-clock time) is the practical replay detector', but duration_s is computed without reference to the loop index, so all three durations are always equal and the detector can never fire.
`exc` names two different things in one function: the caught exception (`except Exception as exc`) and later an excerpt dict (`for exc in assembled_excerpts`).

receipt.py carries a four-line justification for importing the private _extract_post_image_lines while verify.py imports the same function with no comment, so the rationale lives in exactly one of the two call sites.
The 100-entry cap only applies to the beyond-max_line branch; the in-range loop appends without limit, so a large sparse post-image can inline every missing line into the message.
